messages:
emma: heads up — `npm audit` flagged a tar path-traversal CVE (affects extract) in console-ui's dependency tree. snippet below.

emma: ```
{
  "advisories": {
    "1234": {
      "module_name": "tar",
      "cves": ["CVE-2025-0001"],
      "severity": "moderate",
      "findings": [ { "version": "6.1.9", "path": "console-ui > @parcel/core > tar" } ]
    }
  }
}
```

raj: is this reachable from production bundles or only during build?

zoe: looks like it's pulled in by our devtooling (parcel/rollup) but the vulnerable function is only used during extraction of tarballs at build time. we don't ship extract code to clients. low exploitability at runtime, but can be abused in CI runners that extract user-provided archives.

mike: ok so attack surface = CI and developer machines. still needs fast resolution because some infra runs as shared runner with broader permissions.

lina: lockfile churn concern: if we bump tar everywhere we'll get a mega PR across console-ui + shared-components + infra packages. CI will re-run big matrix, and changelog will explode. any ideas to minimize churn? :grimacing:

zoe: we can add a top-level pnpm override (we're on pnpm) to force tar@6.1.11, then run `pnpm install` and only commit pnpm-lock.yaml change; avoids touching package.json per-package.

emma: sample override:```json
{
  "pnpm": {
    "overrides": {
      "tar": "6.1.11"
    }
  }
}
```

mike: ^ that's safer than touching many package.jsons. we should still run build + storybook + smoke tests. i'll run a local canary on my branch.

raj: any reason not to use npm-force-resolutions or yarn-resolutions? we want a consistent approach across repos (some repos use npm, some pnpm).

lina: for legacy npm repos we can add `overrides` in package.json (npm >=8.3 supports it) or use `npm-force-resolutions` as a last resort. ops/infra should coordinate so we don't have multiple conflicting strategies.

sec-bot: created sec ticket SEC-2025-042 linking this thread and assigning priority: P2 (CI RCE surface). recommended action: apply override, run CI, backport if tests fail. https://redwood.internal/SEC-2025-042

emma: proposed timeline: today — add pnpm override + open PR; tomorrow — run full CI/metrics and canary on staging; friday — merge & backport to release branch if green. objections?

zoe: +1. also add note in PR about lockfile churn rationale and include `pnpm why tar` output.

mike: volunteering to do the PR today after stand. I'll paste the `pnpmfile.js`/override in the PR and attach `pnpm why` & `npm audit` output.

lina: ops: after merge, let's rotate any CI runner tokens that had broad filesystem access just in case. small step but worth doing.

raj: good call. if we detect any CI extractions of untrusted archives in the last 30 days we should audit logs. can someone add that to the ticket?

emma: adding audit task now in SEC-2025-042. thanks everyone. :thumbsup:

mike: quick question — do we need a formal security advisory to customers? my read: no, internal only, because exploit requires CI access. open to discussion.

zoe: agree internal notice only, but flag in release notes as "dependency security updates" for transparency.

sec-bot: note: mark SEC-2025-042 as "in progress".

emma: will update thread when PR is open. end.
